'''Evelyn Shaw-Wertheim''' ({{nee}} Steinberg; January 19, 1927 – May 19, 2003) was an American [[ethologist]], children's writer, and caterer. A 1963 [[Guggenheim Fellow]], she wrote several books on ethology, some of which were aimed at children. She worked as a curator at the [[American Museum of Natural History]] and was a professor at [[Stanford University]].

==Biography==
Shaw was born on January 19, 1927, in [[Jersey City, New Jersey]];<ref name="GF"/> her parents were immigrants from Poland.<ref name="Delgado 2003"/> She studied at [[New York University]], where she obtained her BA in 1947 and MS at 1948.<ref name="GF"/> She joined [[Rutgers University]] as an assistant biologist in 1947, before being promoted to assistant instructor in biology (1951–1953) and to instructor (1953–1954).<ref name="GF"/> She obtained her PhD from NYU in 1952.<ref name="GF"/> She was a 1955–1957 [[United States Public Health Service]] postdoctoral fellow.<ref name="GF"/>

After serving as a guest investigator (1952–1955), she formally joined the [[American Museum of Natural History]] (AMNH) as a research associate in 1957, before being promoted to associate curator in 1963.<ref name="GF"/> She also directed the museum's undergraduate research program.<ref name="GF"/> Serving in the Department of Animal Behavior, her curator work included the Hall of Man.<ref name="Delgado 2003"/>

In addition to the AMNH, she served as a lecturer at Rutgers in 1956, before serving as an adjunct assistant professor of vertebrate zoology for a few months at [[Columbia University]] in 1960.<ref name="GF"/> She later moved to [[Stanford University]], where she worked as a biology professor.<ref name="Delgado 2003"/> She once worked at the [[Exploratorium]] as a consultant for [[Frank Oppenheimer]].<ref name="Delgado 2003"/>

As a biologist, Shaw studied fish [[ethology]], with her field research taking place throughout places like Italy and the Bahamas, as well as at the [[Scripps Institution of Oceanography]].<ref name="Delgado 2003"/> She and Joan Darling, a close associate at Stanford, co-authored a book on female ethology titled ''Female Strategies'',<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.newspapers.com/image/127913972/|title=Do animals know about feminism?|first=Harry|last=Eagar|page=4C|date=February 10, 1985|work=The Des Moines Register|via=Newspapers.com|archive-date=January 7, 2026|access-date=December 25, 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260107195207/https://www.newspapers.com/image/127913972/|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.newspapers.com/image/846077975/|work=The Peninsula Times Tribune|date=February 4, 1985|page=B2|via=Newspapers.com|title=Women can find ammunition in animals' behavior also|first=Mary Ann|last=Seawell|archive-date=January 7, 2026|access-date=December 25, 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260107195207/https://www.newspapers.com/image/846077975/|url-status=live}}</ref> and she co-edited ''Advances in the Study of Behavior''.<ref name="GF"/> She also wrote several children's books on ethology, including ''Elephant Seal Island'', ''Fish Out of School'', and ''A Nest of Wood Ducks''.<ref name="Delgado 2003"/> In 1963,<ref>{{Cite web |title=Evelyn Shaw |url=https://www.gf.org/fellows/evelyn-shaw/ |access-date=December 25, 2025 |website=Guggenheim Fellowships |archive-date=October 4, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251004000833/https://www.gf.org/fellows/evelyn-shaw |url-status=live }}</ref> she was awarded a [[Guggenheim Fellowship]] "for a study of the phenomenon of schooling in fishes".<ref name="GF">{{Cite book |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=2o_WAAAAMAAJ |title=Reports of the President and the Treasurer |date=1963 |publisher=John Simon Guggenheim Memorial Foundation |page=69 |archive-date=January 25, 2025 |access-date=December 25, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250125113804/https://books.google.com/books?id=2o_WAAAAMAAJ |url-status=live }}</ref> She also received a USPHS Research Career Development Award that same year.<ref name="GF"/>

Originally married to James Shaw from 1949 until their divorce in 1959 or 1960, Shaw's second marriage was to Frederick Wertheim, lasting from 1970 until her death.<ref name="Delgado 2003"/> Originally a resident of New York City in 1959,<ref name="JJ 1959">{{cite news |date=July 16, 1959 |title=Pretty Zoologist Angles for Fish Story |url=https://www.newspapers.com/image/1192082680/ |work=The Jersey Journal |page=6 |via=Newspapers.com |archive-date=January 7, 2026 |access-date=December 25, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260107195207/https://www.newspapers.com/image/1192082680/ |url-status=live }}</ref> she had lived in San Francisco since 1970.<ref name="Delgado 2003"/> She and Wertheim worked in the catering business, with the latter running the Fred Wertheim Experience, which once appeared on [[John Loring (designer)|John Loring]]'s ''The Tiffany Wedding''.<ref name="Delgado 2003"/><ref>{{cite news |date=June 5, 2016 |title=Frederick D. Wertheim |url=https://www.newspapers.com/image/1223079737/ |work=San Francisco Chronicle |page=C7 |via=Newspapers.com |archive-date=January 7, 2026 |access-date=December 25, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260107195207/https://www.newspapers.com/image/1223079737/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

Shaw had three children.<ref name="Delgado 2003"/> Delgado noted that "as one of only a handful of women in the field of biology in the 1950s", her [[work–life balance]] involved raising a family.<ref name="Delgado 2003"/> She also did part-time work while attending NYU.<ref name="Delgado 2003"/>

Shaw died on May 19, 2003, at her San Francisco home, aged 76, following her battle with cancer.<ref name="Delgado 2003">{{cite news |last=Delgado |first=Ray |date=May 23, 2003 |title=Children's writer, biologist Evelyn Shaw-Wertheim |url=https://www.newspapers.com/image/1244892424/ |work=San Francisco Chronicle |page=A26 |via=Newspapers.com |archive-date=December 25, 2025 |access-date=December 25, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251225234342/https://www.newspapers.com/image/1244892424/ |url-status=live }}</ref> Her archives are located at the [[University of Minnesota]]'s [[Children's Literature Research Collection (Minneapolis)|Children's Literature Research Collection]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Collection: Evelyn Shaw Papers |url=https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/4/resources/2995 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241117161705/https://archives.lib.umn.edu/repositories/4/resources/2995 |archive-date=November 17, 2024 |access-date=December 25, 2025 |website=University of Minnesota Archival Collections Guides}}</ref>
